newsitem.title: SYRIA: China to build syria's biggest cotton spinning mill.
newsitem.headline: China to build syria's biggest cotton spinning mill.

text.p: A Chinese textile company on Wednesday signed a $182.5 million contract with the Syrian government to build a cotton spinning mill on the Syrian coast, officials said.
"The plant which would have a capacity of spinning 24,000 tonnes of ginned cotton would be Syria's biggest mill," said Syria's Industry Minister Ahmed Nezamuldin, who attended the signing ceremony.
He told Reuters the mill's production would be assigned for export.

The contract was signed by Bei Ya Long, president of China's Textile Industrial Corporation for Foreign Economic and Technical Cooperation, which will build the mill, and Hussein Zu'bi, manager of Syria's Textile Institution.
Construction at the Mediterranean city of Jableh some 300 km northwest of Damascus, will start as soon as the Syrian government ratifies it. It should be completed in 30 months.

"The project constitutes a step towards implementing the government's policy of manufacturing all Syria's production of cotton locally and to limit the export of ginned cotton," the Syrian industry minister said.

"As you know, Syria's cotton industry is very old and it is developing rapidly, especially after the expansion in the lands which are planted with cotton...Our production last year reached a record 670,000 tonnes of raw cotton," he said.
"The production capacity of this project makes it not only the biggest project in Syria but also one of the biggest in the region," the minister said.
"We will seek to export the whole production of this mill which would be a very good quality with international standard," he said.
Textile industry sources say the mill is one of several projects that would be built by the private and public sectors during the next three years at a cost of $1.27 billion.
The sources say the capacity of existing mills in Syria is 80,000 tonnes a year, which means the rest of the ginned production which stands at over 280,000 tonnes is being exported.
They said the government had recently allowed the private sector to engage in the spinning industry, which was limited to the government in the past.

The sources said the Industry Ministry had approved 107 textile projects for the private sector at a cost of $675 million while the government will spend about $600 million to renovate or build spinning plants in the country.
